title: Why the Sky-Spire Will Not Be Climbed
text: It is said that when the heavens set down the mountains, they kept one for themselves — a single black needle of stone with no foothold, no path, and no summit that mortal eyes have ever seen. The Jade Emperor forbade its climbing. Since then, a cultivator every century or so has tried anyway. Of those, most have never come down at all. The few that did described the same thing: that halfway up, the wind asks you your true name — and if you answer, you do not belong to yourself afterward.

title: The Fall of the Jadestep Sect
text: The Jadestep Sect stood three hundred years on the hanging terraces. Its founder, Patriarch Mingshu, was a sword-saint who refused to teach until he had lived four decades in silence; when at last he spoke, he drew nine students to him, each the most promising of their age. The sect fell in a single night. A spirit-beast descended from the peak — four-eyed, cloud-flanked, what the survivors (there were no survivors) would have called a 'gale tiger.' Nineteen cultivators lay between it and the tenth student, the youngest, who had not yet cut his first sword-scar. When morning came, only one figure was still standing: the Patriarch, translucent, kneeling by the unfinished scar. Four centuries on, the wind has not finished taking him.

title: Song of the Stormwarden
text:
I do not hold the pass with a sword.
I hold it with a question.
Who are you, under the weight of your qi?
If the answer is long, turn back.
If the answer is short, turn back.
If the answer is a name you earned by walking,
you may pass — and the wind will weigh that, too.

title: The Eight-Pointed Star
text: The Heavenly Sword Tower burn an eight-pointed star into the brows of their disciples at the second initiation. Outside the sect, the brand is a safe-conduct — any tower swordsman may pass a tower holding, unchallenged. Inside it, the brand is a debt. No disciple graduates the tower until the star has been paid off in blood. They have not begun paying the Sky-Spire's debt yet; most of their disciples there are still counting out the interest.
